title: How Toyota Really Makes Money (From Weaving Looms to World No. 1)
description:
Toyota began with a weaving loom that stopped itself when a thread broke. In 2025 the Toyota group sold a record 11.3 million vehicles, more than any other car maker for the sixth year in a row. In this file we open the money machine behind Toyota: Sakichi Toyoda's looms, the jump to cars, the 1950 crisis that almost broke the company, the famous Toyota Production System, the Corolla and the Prius, where the profit really comes from, the tariff shock, and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: Toyota Motor Corporation financial results for the fiscal year ended March 2026 and for the first half of the fiscal year ending March 2027; Toyota 75-year history; Toyota UK and Toyota USA newsrooms (Corolla, hybrid milestones); Lean Enterprise Institute (Toyota Production System); Wikipedia (Sakichi Toyoda, Kiichiro Toyoda); Jiji Press; Nippon.com; Carscoops; The Nation Thailand.

All figures are rounded. Regional operating income excludes valuation gains and losses on swaps, as reported by Toyota. The tariff cost figure is as reported in the press. Forecasts are company guidance. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
